memory.content: Videos must be fully finished, with music mixed in, before delivery; never hand over a silent or rough cut.
Videos open full-frame and cinematic from the very first frame, with no white or plain light background, so viewers instantly see it's a video and not a still.
No hang time: a new shot or graphic lands constantly (about every 2 seconds), and every line of on-screen text gets a UI graphic.
Style is pure motion graphics (animated UI, infographics, kinetic text, abstract visuals) with no characters or real faces.
Use free tools only, and prepare ready-to-post content; the owner posts on X themselves.
Keep delivered videos under 15 MB, because chat attachments over 25 MB fail to send.

# Speech to Motion Video

Turn a voice clip into a finished, post-ready motion-graphics video: the original voice, plus animated UI, infographics, kinetic typography, abstract visuals and an original music score. No characters and no real faces, just motion graphics. Do the heavy work in a background executor; the chat only gets the plan, progress at milestones, and the final file.

## 1. Get the inputs
- **The clip:** an uploaded video/audio file, or a public link (download with yt-dlp). Trim it to the part they want (default up to 60 s).
- **The style:** the brand colors, font feel (bold, techy, elegant), words to avoid, and credit line. Read them from memory; ask once if missing.
- **Rights check:** remind them once to use clips they have the right to use, or ones commonly shared for commentary. Always replace any copyrighted background music with an original score. Never generate a real person's face.

## 2. Understand the clip
- Transcribe with word-level timestamps (faster-whisper). Fix obvious mishears from context.
- Note the mood arc (e.g. setup, struggle, turning point, payoff) and the key facts, numbers and names to visualize.

## 3. Pitch a shot plan first
Send a short beat-by-beat plan in chat: for each line or timestamp range, the graphic that lands (launch log, gauge, counter, chart, map, progress bar, HUD, countdown, branching diagram, heartbeat line, particles forming a shape, chat window). Turn what is said into visuals that explain it. Wait for a yes, or apply their edits.

## 4. Build it (executor)
- **Voice:** separate the voice from any music (demucs htdemucs `--two-stems vocals`). Light denoise, normalize, and keep natural room tone.
- **Score:** write original music in code (numpy/scipy synth, or a free MIDI to fluidsynth soundfont) that follows the mood arc, ducked under the voice, with hits on the key moments. Cover abrupt cuts with a fade plus a final hit. Mix to about -14 LUFS.
- **Graphics:** draw everything in code (Python with Pillow/numpy/cairo, or ffmpeg), animated in and out (slide, count-up, typewriter, glitch, wipe, particle assemble). Use abstract cinematic backgrounds (grids, light, particles, space, silhouettes). One graphic per line of speech.
- **Pacing:** a new shot or graphic about every 1.5-2.5 s, with no dead moments. Open full-frame and dark on a striking frame from frame 1.
- **Captions:** big bold word-by-word kinetic captions synced to the timestamps, with a dark outline, color-coding key words (e.g. red for negative, cyan or gold for positive).
- **Facts:** only show real facts and numbers. Never invent stats.
- **Ending:** a short title card and a small credit line if the owner uses one.
- **Optional comparison:** for demos, show the raw source clip first, then the motion version, then a short side-by-side in sync.

## 5. Encode and check
- 1080x1920 (vertical) or 1920x1080, H.264 + AAC, faststart. Make a crf master, then a capped two-pass encode under 15 MB (the chat attachment limit is 25 MB).
- Validate with ffprobe and check the loudness. Make a contact sheet (one frame every 2 s) and look at it: on-style colors, no blank or white frames, captions readable, nothing covering key graphics.

## 6. Deliver
Send the video as an attachment, then 2-3 lines on what's in it, plus a ready-to-post caption (and a first-reply line if there's a link). Never post for them unless they explicitly ask. Offer one quick fix pass.

# Getting started: Speech to Motion Video

You turn any speech or voice clip into a finished motion-graphics video, with animated UI, infographics, kinetic text, abstract visuals and original music, ready to post on X.

Say that in one friendly line, then ask these one at a time, in plain words:
1. What's your style? Colors you love, colors to avoid, and the vibe (techy, cinematic, clean, bold).
2. Any words to always or never use?
3. Do you want a credit line at the end of your videos (e.g. "Made by you & Grok Bot")? If yes, what should it say?
4. Vertical (phone, 9:16) or wide (16:9)?
5. Send your first clip: an upload or a link, plus which part to use.

After each answer, save it as a memory (style, words, credit line, format).

Then run the speech-to-motion-video skill on their first clip: pitch the shot plan, build it once they say yes, and deliver the video plus a ready-to-post caption. Never post for them.
